content.user_title: Design Data Science Experiments and Models
content.value_statement: Data science projects often lack clear experiment plans and evaluation checks. This skill provides structured guidance for experiments, features, models, and analytics decisions.
actual_capabilities: Guides experiment design with production, reliability, observability, and privacy considerations.
Summarizes advanced statistical methods, feature engineering patterns, and ML system practices.
Provides scaffold Python scripts for experiment design, feature engineering, and model evaluation workflows.
Supports planning for model monitoring, drift detection, deployment, and retraining practices.
Helps convert analytical work into stakeholder-ready recommendations and trade-off discussions.
limitations: The included scripts are scaffolds and do not implement real modeling or data transformation logic.
It needs user-provided data context, metrics, constraints, and business goals.
It does not validate statistical assumptions without actual data or experiment results.
Deployment commands are examples and should not run without explicit review.

use_cases.title: Plan A/B Tests
use_cases.description: Create hypotheses, metrics, guardrails, sample requirements, and rollout checks for product experiments.

use_cases.title: Review Feature Pipelines
use_cases.description: Evaluate feature quality, leakage risk, monitoring needs, and reproducibility before model training.

use_cases.title: Explain Model Results
use_cases.description: Prepare concise model evaluation summaries with limitations, trade-offs, and next steps for stakeholders.

prompt_templates.title: Beginner Experiment Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when defining a first test plan.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to draft an A/B test plan for [change], primary metric [metric], audience [audience], and risk [risk].

prompt_templates.title: Feature Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these proposed features for leakage, missingness, drift, and monitoring needs: [feature list].

prompt_templates.title: Model Evaluation Brief
prompt_templates.scenario: Use after training or comparing models.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a model evaluation brief for [model], metrics [metrics], validation approach [approach], and business decision [decision].

prompt_templates.title: Advanced Causal Analysis
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when observational data drives a decision.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a causal analysis for [question], treatment [treatment], outcome [outcome], confounders [confounders], and identification concerns.

output_examples.input: A product team wants to test a new checkout flow with revenue and conversion goals.
output: Experiment plan with hypothesis, primary metric, guardrails, segmentation, and stopping rules.
Risk review covering novelty effects, sample contamination, and operational monitoring.

output_examples.input: A machine learning team has candidate features for churn prediction.
output: Feature review covering leakage, freshness, missing data, drift, and reproducibility.
Prioritized recommendations for feature removal, monitoring, and validation.

output_examples.input: An executive needs a clear summary of model performance before launch.
output: Stakeholder brief with performance, business impact, limitations, and launch decision points.
Recommended follow-up checks for monitoring, fairness, and retraining.

best_practices: Provide the business goal, metric definitions, data source, and decision owner before asking for analysis.
Ask for assumptions, risks, and validation checks whenever the output supports a production decision.
Review any suggested command or deployment step before running it in a real environment.
anti_patterns: Do not treat scaffold script output as a completed statistical analysis.
Do not ask for causal claims without sharing assumptions, confounders, and identification strategy.
Do not run deployment examples against live systems without explicit approval and environment review.

faq.question: Does this skill train machine learning models?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and scaffold scripts, but it does not implement complete training logic.

faq.question: Can it help with A/B testing?
faq.answer: Yes. It can structure hypotheses, metrics, guardrails, sample planning, and interpretation checks.

faq.question: Does it work with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What inputs improve the results?
faq.answer: Share business goals, data sources, metric definitions, constraints, and current analysis results.

faq.question: Are the shell commands required?
faq.answer: No. They are documentation examples and should be reviewed before any manual use.

faq.question: Is it suitable for regulated data?
faq.answer: Use it only with approved data handling practices, privacy controls, and organization-specific compliance review.
